content.intro: This lesson covers Data Model Optimization and Validation as part of Data Models, Power Pivot, and DAX. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Data Model Optimization and Validation supports repeatable analysis by organizing, cleaning, summarizing, or relating data. Preserve the raw source and reconcile a summary back to its input records. Compatibility: Power Query, the Data Model, Power Pivot and DAX are related but distinct capabilities; their exact availability varies by Excel edition, operating system, license and update channel. Follow the course’s local availability checklist before building a dependent workflow.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Data Model Optimization and Validation focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Removing unnecessary columns and rows; Choosing suitable data types; Checking relationships and totals; Balancing usability, model size, and performance. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

items: Balancing usability, model size, and performance

content_blocks.expected_output: Measure expression for total amount in a Data Model table named Sales with a numeric Amount column. The table and column names must match the model.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Create a measure in the Data Model/Power Pivot measure editor, then compare it with an independently calculated total. Availability varies by Excel edition/platform.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for data model optimization and validation. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates data model optimization and validation. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates data model optimization and validation; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Measure expression for total amount in a Data Model table named Sales with a numeric Amount column. The table and column names must match the model.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Data Model Optimization and Validation supports the workflow in Data Models, Power Pivot, and DAX.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
